deep.reconstruction:
Setting, continued from the previous page. S = Spec W, with W a complete DVR (Witt vectors) and s_0 its closed point. X_0 is proper and smooth over k and sits as the fibre at a point t_0 (over s_0) of a proper smooth family f: Y -> M, with h: M -> S of finite type (a 'modular' family). Each section g of h through t_0 gives a lifting X_g of X_0 to S. Put K = Rf_*(Ω^•_{Y/M}), the relative de Rham complex, so that in good cases Rf_{g*}(Ω^•_{X_g/S}) ≅ g^*K.

This page states the key observation. For the various sections g prolonging t_0, the complexes g^*K are canonically isomorphic to one another in the derived category. Hence the g^*(H^i), with H^i = H^i(K) = R^if_*(Ω^•_{Y/M}), are canonically isomorphic modulo torsion (base change for individual cohomology sheaves needs torsion-freeness). So the de Rham cohomology of a lifting depends only on X_0.

Grothendieck then reinterprets this. A transitive system of isomorphisms g^*E ≅ g'^*E between pullbacks of a Module E on M (near t_0, relative to S) is a 'stratification' of E relative to S. He remarks that one 'should say descent': such a structure is like descent data for E along h. The effective case would be E ≅ h^*(E_0) for a Module E_0 on S, which obviously gives such a transitive system.

The next page lists the planned sections:
- general definition of stratification and its relation with connections;
- the transitive system of isomorphisms it furnishes over a complete local base;
- the Gauss–Manin connection.

This is the motivating introduction of the IHES lectures 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (1966–67, notes by I. Coates and O. Jussila, published in Dix exposés, 1968). The goal is to show that H_dR of a lift is a crystal on X_0 and to arrive at crystalline cohomology.
errors: The canonical isomorphism between the g^*K is only plausible for sections that agree with t_0 to sufficient p-adic order. It comes from integrating the Gauss–Manin connection (Taylor series), whose convergence needs divided powers / p-adic topological nilpotence. The page states it without these hypotheses; Grothendieck fills this in later in the notes.
The marginal insertion '= R^if_*(Ω^•_{Y/M})' attached to the complexes g^*(K) should refer to K = Rf_*, not to R^if_*. This is a slip of placement.
'Modulo torsion' is overly cautious. Crystalline theory (Berthelot) gives integral canonical isomorphisms at the level of complexes; torsion matters only for the individual H^i under base change.

ideas.what: De Rham cohomology of a lifting of X_0 to W is independent of the lifting, canonically: the pullbacks g^*Rf_*Ω^•_{Y/M} along different sections of a moduli family are canonically isomorphic.
ideas.modern_name: Crystalline nature of de Rham cohomology / comparison H_cris(X_0/W) ≅ H_dR(X/W)
ideas.where_published: 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes', Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas (1968), introduction

ideas.what: A transitive system of isomorphisms between the g^*E viewed as a stratification, i.e. as descent data along M -> S.
ideas.modern_name: Stratification (Grothendieck): isomorphisms p_1^*E ≅ p_2^*E on the formal neighbourhood of the diagonal, satisfying a cocycle condition; equivalent to descent along M -> M/S_inf (de Rham stack)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (1966–68); Berthelot for the PD version; Simpson for de Rham stack language
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (Dix exposés); Berthelot, Cohomologie cristalline (LNM 407)

ideas.what: The Gauss–Manin connection as the source of the transitive isomorphisms.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of the well-known published motivation for crystals and stratifications. The remark 'on devrait dire descente' anticipates the de Rham-stack viewpoint, but stratification as descent along the infinitesimal neighbourhood is already implicit in the published 1968 text.

The image reads 'g^*(K^•), pour les différentes sections g de M sur S prolongeant t_0, sont canoniquement isomorphes entre eux'; 'canoniquement isomorphes' appears on the later line for g^*(H^i), and the first instance reads more like 'sont canoniquement' / 'sont isomorphes'.
'stratification [?] hyper-générale [?]' is doubtful; the handwriting looks more like 'une structure ...'. It is uncertain.
